headline: Pretrained protein models paired with explicit training-data and objective choices
label: Context Conditioned Biomolecular Prediction
summary: Recent preprints and papers add augmentation, domain-adversarial alignment, and reinforcement learning to pretrained biomolecular language models.
synthesis: Across these items, the dominant thread is conditioning pretrained or learned representations on explicit choices about data, objectives, or domain. Augmentation strategies target protein language model performance on small protein sets, including ESM-3 generated complexes. Neopep couples a sequence-conditioned diffusion model, pretrained on PDB, with reinforcement learning driven by machine-learned force field energy for non-canonical peptides. PRIDA applies conditional domain-adversarial learning to pretrained protein and RNA language models, while PDI-Spot uses structure- and sequence-derived residue embeddings to identify protein-DNA hotspots. The quantum Wasserstein GAN extends this pattern to latent-space molecule generation. What is new is treating data construction, training objectives, and domain alignment as explicit constraints rather than incidental settings. The evidence is abstract-level only, so claimed performance requires verification against full results.
